title: Travels through France and Italy
author: Tobias Smollett
description: The Scottish novelist Tobias Smollett spent two winters in Nice in the 1760s for his health and wrote about it in grumpy, detailed letters. His book helped bring the first British winter visitors.

title: Tender Is the Night
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Fitzgerald’s novel about a glamorous American couple on the Riviera in the 1920s and the slow collapse of their marriage. It draws on the summers he and Zelda spent on the coast west of Nice.

title: Promise at Dawn
author: Romain Gary
description: Romain Gary’s memoir of his mother, who brought him from Vilnius to Nice and ran a small boarding house here in the 1930s, convinced he would become a great man. He became a war hero and a famous novelist.

title: Matisse the Master
author: Hilary Spurling
description: The second volume of Hilary Spurling’s biography covers Matisse’s years in Nice, from his arrival in 1917 to the paper cut-outs he made in bed at the Régina at the end of his life.

title: J’Accuse: The Dark Side of Nice
author: Graham Greene
description: A short pamphlet in which novelist Graham Greene, who lived in nearby Antibes, accused Nice’s political establishment of protecting organized crime. It was banned in France for a time.

title: Côte d’Azur: Inventing the French Riviera
author: Mary Blume
description: Journalist Mary Blume’s lively history of how the coast became the Riviera: British invalids, Russian grand dukes, American millionaires, artists, and the summer crowds that followed.
